rationale: Verbal form possibly derived from Greek τάσσω-root (cf. accumulated ⲧⲁⲝⲣⲟ 'establish'). In the dialogue context here it functions as a verb of disciple-inquiry. Could alternatively be 'said' (variant of ⲡⲧⲁⲭⲉ).

Tentatively read as Lycopolitan ⲡⲣ̄ⲉ = ⲡⲏⲣⲉ 'wonder, marvel' with ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ 'of heart.' The compound 'wonder/marvel of heart' would name the inward astonishment that the disciple has experienced upon perceiving Sophia.

Lycopolitan verb of setting/abiding, paralleled by ⲥⲕⲁⲁⲧ 'lies set' in line 22. Possibly a causative-reflexive on ⲧⲱⲃⲉ 'seal' or a related abiding-root. The verb names the state of Sophia resting within the heart, contrasted with her extending forth in proclamation.

Discourse-marker introducing the disciple's secondary observation in line 8 (the manner of his inward perception of Sophia). Etymology unclear; possibly contracted form of πάλιν or compound on ⲥⲟⲛ 'time, occasion.'
1sg form, possibly ⲉ-(ⲉ)ⲓ- + ⲙⲏⲧ 'midst' or qualitative of a verb of approach. Construction ⲉⲓⲙⲏⲧ ⲁⲡⲥⲁⲡ 'I am at/draw near to the time' fits temporal-proximity sense. Confidence low.

Compound: ⲣ̄- ('do') + ϩⲟⲩⲟ ('excess, more') + ⲁⲓⲉⲩⲧⲉ ('extend, become long,' in glossary). 'Do excess-extending' = extend abundantly/grow forth more. Captures Sophia's proclamation-amplified dilation.

Causative ⲧⲣ̄- + ⲟⲩⲁⲛⲉ (likely Lycopolitan reflex of ⲟⲩⲱⲛϩ 'manifest'). The recipient of Sophia's proclamation 'causes-manifestation' in her — i.e., further reveals her actively. Preserves the active-emission verbal quality.

proposed_english: she shall give birth to him
rationale: Lycopolitan compound ⲥ-ⲁ-ⲭⲡⲟ-ϥ 'she-shall-beget-him' (3sg.f future + ⲭⲡⲟ 'beget,' Lyc. for ϫⲡⲟ; cf. ⲧⲟⲓⲛⲭⲧⲟ in glossary). The mother's act of birthing the child in the parable's culmination.
Lycopolitan qualitative of ⲱϫ 'be joined.' Modifies ⲙⲉⲗⲟⲥ 'members': 'members joined to him' = the newborn complete with all his members attached in their proper places.
